## The Rule

The owner's rule: “If they are reported in order, then each one should be recorded as a result, as long as each one is stronger than the last. If a stronger result is reported first, then the other one should not be recorded since it is weaker after that, unless there is some key reason it should be recorded.”

At each count the standing side starts at the record on `main`, frozen by `gather` in [starts.yaml](starts.yaml) and never read from the working tree. For n ≤ 324 it is the set of both upper lanes of the case record (`packing/frontier/n-NNN.md`): each lane's exact form where that is rational, a rigorous 90-digit interval where it is a closed form with square roots, an enclosure by exact sign change of the root a `root(...)` form names, else its printed value within one unit of its last place; with any register entry pending adoption that states a smaller bound, and only the members nothing else is decidably below. Above 324 it is the current beyond-horizon row of `frontier/source-coverage.yaml`, else the grid ⌈√n⌉. The claims are then taken in the order they reached this repository: issue, comment or pull-request creation, the update comment for a claim added to an issue later, the commit for a claim added to a pull request later, and the first commit for a publication in a watched repository that no issue reports. A claim is recorded when every number it may be is below every number every member of the standing side may be, and it becomes the standing side. A claim equal to a member (a tie: the earlier holder keeps it) or above one is not recorded, and the table names what holds the count. A comparison the printed precision cannot decide is undecided; the undecided claim stays beside the standing side until a claim is decidably below both. Exact sides come from the lanes' frozen claim records or, where `ledger.yaml` says so, from the certificate at its pinned commit; this ledger compares sides and verifies no certificate. Where a lane's claim record or an exact decision's receipt states how a claim compares with a record lane or a pending register entry, that relation decides in place of the prints while the record still prints what it read (`record_relations` in `ledger.yaml`, each naming where it was read). Sides are shown rounded up at 12 places where exact, as printed otherwise.

## Counts

1 claims at 1 counts. Recorded: 1 new packings (of which 1 continue another holder's or the reporter's own arrangement), 0 refinements of a standing packing, 0 that no source classifies; 0 recorded by exception; 0 not recorded; 0 undecided.

A refinement is the same configuration with a tighter certificate (a padding reduction, an exact-contact refinement, an exact attainment), as a source says; a new packing is one its source says is new, including one a continued search found from another arrangement. The rule records both; the register credits a refinement as a regularization of the packing it tightens.

## Owner Decisions Needed

Nothing here is decided by the rule; each list is what the owner may want to rule on.

### Publication in a Watched Repository

By default a certificate published in a watched repository, with no issue, competes as a report from its first commit. These are the counts where a verdict changes if such publications are not counted: each publication drops out of the walk, and a later report may then be recorded in its place.

None.

### Key-Reason Candidates

Claims an argument says have a key reason to be recorded. The rule does not apply it: the verdict is the rule's, and the owner decides.

None.
